extracted.intended_audience: users/programmers who create technical figures with MetaPost (TeX/troff users, graphics programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Authoring MetaPost source to produce vector/bitmap figures for inclusion in TeX/troff or web documents; includes rules for syntax, path construction, linear equations, data types, output formats, and workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default coordinate system and units
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost uses the same default coordinate system as PostScript: (30,0) means 30 units to the right of the origin where a unit is a PostScript point (1/72 inch). MetaPost recognizes unit names bp, pt, in, pc, cm, mm, cc, dd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may omit units for zero (0) or use explicit units like 2cm. Use consistent units; conversions like 2cm are parsed as 2*cm. Prefer using an explicit scale factor (see 'Use of scale factor u') when you want to change drawing scale without affecting unrelated quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a user-defined scale factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a variable (e.g., u) as a scale factor and use it in coordinates so the entire drawing can be rescaled by changing u (for example u = 1cm or u = 0.5cm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives control over what gets scaled and what does not so that changing u will not affect features such as line widths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pen selection and pickup
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the pen used for subsequent draw or drawdot statements with pickup ⟨pen expression⟩; commonly pencircle scaled ⟨size⟩ determines pen thickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: pickup pencircle scaled 4pt sets a fairly large pen (~8× default). Other pen shapes (elliptical, polygonal) can be used for calligraphic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic drawing statements and joins (--, .., ...)
rubrics_metrics.description: draw (a)--(b) draws straight segments; draw p..q..r draws smooth (cubic Bézier) curves through points; path joins can mix -- and .. and you can append ..cycle to close a curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use -- for polygonal segments, .. for smooth cubic interpolation, and ... (three dots) when you want to avoid inflection points when possible. You can mix for complex shapes (e.g., draw z0..z1..z2..z3--z4--cycle).

rubrics_metrics.name: beginfig/endfig structure and final end
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost input normally contains beginfig(n); ... endfig; pairs and a final end statement. The numeric argument to beginfig determines the output file index and name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the final end is omitted MetaPost enters interactive mode. Statements outside beginfig...endfig are processed but drawing operations there produce no visible output (useful for global configuration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Output formats and preview considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost outputs PostScript by default, and can produce SVG or PNG when outputformat is changed (e.g., outputformat := "svg").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preview PostScript with GSview/PS_View, SVG/PNG with browsers like Firefox. If graphics contain text labels, additional work (e.g., prologues) may be required to ensure fonts render correctly in PostScript viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: prologues setting for reliable fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Set prologues := 3 when graphics contain text labels to make sure the correct fonts are used under all possible circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This setting embeds font prologues appropriately for downstream viewers and inclusion in documents; see Section 8.1 and 14 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output filename template (outputtemplate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use outputtemplate (an internal string variable) to control naming of output files, e.g., outputtemplate := "%j-%c.mps" yields ⟨jobname⟩-⟨n⟩.mps output names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can change extensions (e.g., .mps) and indexing format. filenametemplate is deprecated; use outputtemplate for newer versions but conditional code can preserve backwards compatibility with older MetaPost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: A percent sign % introduces a comment: the remainder of the current line is ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use % for inline and end-of-line comments in MetaPost source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation operator = versus assignment operator :=
rubrics_metrics.description: '=' declares linear equations to be solved by MetaPost's linear solver; ':=' performs assignment that changes a variable's value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a+b=3; 2a=b+3; are equations solved by the solver. a:=a+1 is the correct way to increment a. '=' is not assignment and a=a+1 is an inconsistent equation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linearity restrictions and handling unknowns
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost only accepts linear equations; you may not multiply two unknown quantities, divide by an unknown, or use an unknown in a draw statement. An expression is legal only if it can be interpreted linearly given known values or deduced differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure differences used as mediation factors are known (or deducible) before using whatever[] or fractional mediation. The system will warn on redundant equations and error on inconsistent equations. Unknowns may sometimes be deduced indirectly, but you cannot perform nonlinear operations on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation expressions and the whatever macro
rubrics_metrics.description: Mediation expressions like 1/3[z3,z6] set a point at a fraction along the segment from z3 to z6. The whatever macro creates anonymous variables (e.g., z20=whatever[z1,z3]=whatever[z2,z4]) to express intersection or unknown fractions without naming auxiliaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mediation for evenly spaced points and whatever to avoid inventing temporary variable names. Be mindful of the linearity requirements when using mediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension parameter for paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Using .. sets tension to the default 1. You can set explicit tension values (tension ⟨numeric⟩) between knots to alter curve tightness; tension may be less than 1 but must be at least 3/4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax examples: draw z0..z1..tension 1.3..z2..z3 and draw z0..z1..tension 1.5 and 1..z2..z3 for asymmetric tension across a join. Increase tension to reduce 'wild' curvature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curl parameter for path endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: The {curl c} direction specifier sets a curl parameter at path endpoints affecting endpoint curvature; small c reduces curvature, large c increases it; c=0 makes curvature approach zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use {curl c} on endpoints: draw z0{curl c}..z1..{curl c}z2. Defaults cause ends to be approximately circular arcs when no directions are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction specifiers for knots
rubrics_metrics.description: Direction specifiers like {dir 45}, {up}, {left}, {right}, {down} can be placed before/after path knots and control incoming/outgoing tangent direction; a direction given on only one side applies to both incoming and outgoing segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can give direction vectors of any length; putting both before and after a knot can create a corner. Example: ..{dir 60}(10,0){up}.. produces a corner at (10,0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Path syntax: controls and explicit control points
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost allows explicit Bézier control points via controls (x,y) and controls (p1) and (p2) pairs; controls specifications may give one or two control points; when only one is given it's applied symmetrically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can mix automatic control-point selection with explicit controls: draw ...controls (26.8,-1.8) and (51.4,14.6)..(60,40).. etc. See summary grammar (Figure 13) for full syntax (--, .., ..., controls, tension, curl).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bézier cubic curve model and continuity guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost constructs piecewise cubic Bézier curves with continuous slope and approximately continuous curvature between knots; the path is parameterized piecewise and the interpreter selects Bézier control points to satisfy continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For precise control use explicit controls or direction/tension/curl specifiers. The selection rules are described in the cited literature (Hobby, METAFONTbook). Use ... to avoid inflections when desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data types available
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost has ten basic data types: numeric, pair, path, transform, (rgb)color, cmykcolor, string, boolean, picture, and pen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand each type's operations: pairs are numeric pairs used for coordinates; paths are first-class objects; transforms apply to pairs, paths, pictures, pens, transforms; pictures accumulate drawing operations (currentpicture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric representation and warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric quantities are fixed-point multiples of epsilon = 1/65536. Numeric values normally must have absolute value less than 4096; intermediate results can be eight times larger. Warnings about large numerics can be suppressed by setting warningcheck to zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For very large magnitudes consider adjusting warningcheck, but typical coordinate ranges (4096 points ≈ 1.4 m) are sufficient for figures. Be aware of roundoff behavior in equation solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color representations and clipping
rubrics_metrics.description: rgbcolor is a triplet (r,g,b) generally between 0 and 1; MetaPost clips color components to [0,1] when adding an object to a picture. cmykcolor is a four-component type (c,m,y,k) with white (0,0,0,0) and black (0,0,0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While any triplet is allowed, output clamps components. Avoid using redundant CMYK specifications that lead to wasted ink (e.g., using both high CMY and K to manufacture black).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pen and picture semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: A pen determines line thickness and calligraphic effects; picture variables hold drawable content. The draw statement stores results in currentpicture unless directed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pickup to select pens and combine pictures with transforms. Pens can be circular (pencircle scaled), elliptical, or polygonal (makepen/makepath).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression syntax and operator precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressions follow four levels of precedence: primary, secondary, tertiary, expression. Operators include primary binops (*, /, **, dotprod), secondary binops (+, - , ++, +-+), tertiary and expression-level operators (and, or, & concatenation, comparison operators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of precedence pitfalls: 3*a**2 means (3*a)**2; -a**2 means (-a)**2 because ** binds at the same precedence as * and unary negation is primary level. Use parentheses to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dot product and Pythagorean operators
rubrics_metrics.description: dotprod computes the vector dot product of two pairs (z1 dotprod z2 = x1*x2 + y1*y2). Operators ++ and +-+ compute Pythagorean addition and subtraction (a++b ≡ sqrt(a^2 + b^2), a+-+b ≡ sqrt(a^2 - b^2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these specialized operators for vector/length calculations rather than expanding manually.

rubrics_metrics.name: String operations and substring indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: String concatenation uses & (e.g., "abc" & "de" → "abcde"). substring ⟨pair⟩ of ⟨string⟩ selects a substring using indices that lie between characters (substring (2,4) of "abcde" → "cd"). length returns number of characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat string indexing as positions between characters (graph-paper model) to avoid off-by-one mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation parsing nuance: numeric atom parenthesization
rubrics_metrics.description: In mediation expressions ⟨numeric atom⟩[a,b] the numeric atom must be parenthesized when it is not just a variable, a positive number, or a positive fraction. For example, -1[a,b] ≠ (-1)[a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit: use parentheses around negative or complex numeric atoms in mediation expressions to ensure the intended parsing and semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: show command and tracingonline
rubrics_metrics.description: show ⟨expression⟩ prints a symbolic representation of the value (numeric values printed with >>). To get full results printed on the terminal set tracingonline to a positive value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use show to debug expressions; pictures produce references pointing to the transcript file. tracingonline helps see full show output interactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error messages, redundancy and roundoff
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost warns about redundant equations ('! Redundant equation.') and errors on inconsistent equations ('! Inconsistent equation (off by ... )'). Roundoff error can occur in linear solving (e.g., intersections of nearly parallel lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you encounter inconsistent or near-inconsistent systems, check for rounding issues and ill-conditioned equations. Use more robust constructions or adjust your constraints to avoid instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command-line invocation and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically invoke MetaPost with mpost ⟨input file⟩ (sometimes mp). The executable is a wrapper around mplib; mplib can be embedded in other applications (e.g., LuaTeX). Compilation produces transcript ⟨jobname⟩.log and output graphic files named ⟨jobname⟩.⟨n⟩ by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Section B.2 for command-line options. Use transcript/log files for error messages and interactive inputs. For inclusion workflows see Sections 14 and the appendices for embedding and preview tips.
